title: SQL injection on login / auth fields
summary: Treat login username/password (or JSON /login body) as an injection surface even when the crawl recorded no query-string params.
steps: Identify the mapped login form or POST /login|/signin|/api/auth/login (JSON body counts).
compare_requests: baseline valid-looking credentials vs one mutation on username, then password — error canary first.
If no SQL error: boolean pair (true vs false condition) on the same field.
If still quiet: timing pair. A delay that scales with SLEEP is SUBMIT with the timing table (same bar as WP tax_query).
generate_injection_payloads(vuln_type='sqli', technique='time_based') and technique='auth_bypass' for mutant values. sqlmap --batch only after a canary.
If WAF/403/timeout: one compare_requests or run_custom_probe rewrite from the defense body, then prove or kill. Do not re-run sqlmap with the same flags.
Auth bypass (session issued from a canary) is Critical. Blind timing without a session is High. Status 200 without a differential is not a finding. No os-shell, no table dump.
pass_signals: Error/boolean/time differential on a named login field
Authenticated session issued from a canary
Timing delta that scales with SLEEP
kill_signals: No anomalous body/timing after error + boolean + timing canaries and one blocked-probe rewrite
